name: Casio PD wave family: saw-pulse, double-sine, pulse, square, and windowed-sync resonance
goal: Expand Casio-style phase distortion beyond the basic saw: derive saw-pulse (sine table), double-sine (warp twice / half-rate), pulse (node at full height with end hold), true square (run the warper twice per cycle), and resonant 'windowed sync' waves (slave sync reset enveloped by a decaying window to remove the click), then thicken with unison.
prerequisites: Ability to sync-reset a higher-rate oscillator and multiply by an amplitude window

inputs.name: wave_mode
inputs.description: saw | saw-pulse | double-sine | pulse | square | resonance

inputs.name: skew_or_y_node
inputs.description: Node height/position control (0.5 for classic saw knee; toward 1.0 for pulse-style full sweep)

outputs.name: cz_style_oscillator
outputs.description: Multi-shape PD oscillator including windowed-sync resonance mode

constraints: Portable signal-flow recipe for Web Audio / Traveler-inspired / any hybrid synth with comparable modules; not affiliated with any vendor.
Do not copy proprietary factory preset banks, wavetable file names, or sample packs; use original/free waves or generic shapes.
Steps and numeric values are grounded only in the YouTube Show-transcript text; approximate where the speaker gestured without stating a number.
Resonance mode is an emulation of sync+window, not a true analog filter resonance; expect formanty decaying-sine character rather than Moog-style Q.

steps.action: Start from the piecewise phase warp (fast then slow read). For the classic saw, use a cosine table with the knee near mid-amplitude (y≈0.5).
steps.expect: Identity warp → cosine; cocked node → saw-like

steps.action: Saw-pulse: swap the cosine table for a sine table under the same warp (first half read fast, second slow) to get the CZ saw-pulse family shape.
steps.expect: Same x1 control yields a different, pulse-tilted spectral contour vs cosine-saw

steps.action: Double-sine: apply the same shaping so one full sine cycle is played fast and the next slow (or conceptually run at half rate with the warp), producing a weird octave/double-sine texture.
steps.expect: Audible octave-ish thickening without a second oscillator

steps.action: Pulse: raise the node height (y-position) toward 1.0 so the fast segment climbs higher and the cycle then waits/holds at the end before resetting — a pulse with end dwell. Cosine or sine both work; Casio often used sine.
steps.expect: Increasing skew/y toward 100% moves from mid-knee saw toward full-height pulse

steps.action: Square: run the warping function twice per cycle (multiply phase by 2 then wrap 0→1 before the piecewise map), i.e. twice-per-cycle instead of once — Casio's fuller square uses the full 100% cycle read this way rather than a weaker half-cycle squish.
steps.expect: Output approaches a square-like duty with the warp still controlling edge sharpness

steps.action: Resonance / windowed-sync: run a higher-rate sine (or oscillator) that is hard-synced/reset by the fundamental, then multiply by a decaying amplitude window each master cycle so the sync gap/click is enveloped away — an exponentially decaying sine burst that mimics filter resonance.
steps.expect: Synced overtones without a hard click; opening the sync ratio brightens like resonance

steps.action: Optional CZ trick: alternate wave shapes cycle-by-cycle (e.g. square then saw) so the ear hears one compound cycle. Add a unison/detune ('fat') layer for organic thickness on leads/pads.
steps.expect: Odd textures from alternation; unison adds weight without changing the PD core

steps.action: Expose skew/y as a continuous 'DCW' macro and modulate it with envelopes for plucky filterless motion; keep pitch from the master phase ramp only.
steps.expect: Envelope on skew opens brightness while pitch stays in key

verification: Each wave_mode produces a distinct scope shape under the same pitch
Resonance mode shows a decaying burst each cycle with no loud sync click
Skew/y automation does not change perceived fundamental pitch
